[[File:Geoffrey West.jpg|thumb]]

'''Geoffrey Brian West''' (born 15 December 1940)<ref name="curr vitae">{{cite web|first=Geoffrey B.|last=West|url=https://sfi-edu.s3.amazonaws.com/sfi-edu/production/uploads/people/resumes/West_CV_2015.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae|website=sfi-edu.s3.amazonaws.com|date=11 June 2014 |accessdate=17 August 2022}}</ref> is a British [[theoretical physicist]] and former president and distinguished professor of the [[Santa Fe Institute]]. He is one of the leading scientists working on a scientific model of [[City|cities]] (see also, [[urban scaling]]). Among other things, his work states that with the doubling of a city's population, salaries per capita will generally increase by 15%.<ref>{{Cite journal
| last1 = Bettencourt | first1 = L. M. A.
| last2 = Lobo | first2 = J.
| last3 = Helbing | first3 = D.
| last4 = Kuhnert | first4 = C.

| authorlink5 = Geoffrey West
| title = Growth, innovation, scaling, and the pace of life in cities
| doi = 10.1073/pnas.0610172104
| journal = Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
| volume = 104
| issue = 17
| pages = 7301–7306
| year = 2007
| pmid = 17438298
| pmc =1852329
| bibcode = 2007PNAS..104.7301B | doi-access = free
}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Born in [[Taunton]], Somerset, a rural town in western England, West moved to London when he was 13.<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.physicscentral.com/explore/people/west.cfm
|title=Geoffrey West
|website=PhysicsCentral
|publisher=American Physical Society
|accessdate=2019-01-27
}}</ref> He received a Bachelor of Arts degree in physics from the [[University of Cambridge]] and pursued [[graduate school|graduate studies]] on the [[pion]] at [[Stanford University]].<ref name="westphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Geoffrey Brian|last=West |title= I. Form Factors of the Three-Body Nuclei II. Coulomb Scattering and the Form Factor of the Pion |publisher=Stanford University |year=1966 |authorlink=Geoffrey West|id={{ProQuest|302188497}}}}</ref>

West became a Stanford faculty member before he joined the particle theory group at [[New Mexico]]'s [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]]. After Los Alamos, he became president of the [[Santa Fe Institute]], where he worked and works on biological issues such as the [[allometry|allometric law]]<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = West | first1 = G. B. | authorlink1 = Geoffrey West| last2 = Brown | first2 = J. H. | last3 = Enquist | first3 = B. J. | doi = 10.1126/science.276.5309.122 | title = A General Model for the Origin of Allometric Scaling Laws in Biology | journal = Science | volume = 276 | issue = 5309 | pages = 122–126 | year = 1997 | pmid =  9082983| s2cid = 3140271 }}</ref> and other [[power law]]s in [[biology]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = West | first1 = G. B. | authorlink1 = Geoffrey West| last2 = Brown | first2 = J. H. | last3 = Enquist | first3 = B. J. | doi = 10.1038/35098076 | title = A general model for ontogenetic growth | journal = Nature | volume = 413 | issue = 6856 | pages = 628–631 | year = 2001 | pmid =  11675785|bibcode = 2001Natur.413..628W | s2cid = 4393103 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Gillooly | first1 = J. F. | last2 = Brown | first2 = J. H. | last3 = West | first3 = G. B. | authorlink3 = Geoffrey West| last4 = Savage | first4 = V. M. | last5 = Charnov | first5 = E. L. | title = Effects of Size and Temperature on Metabolic Rate | doi = 10.1126/science.1061967 | journal = Science | volume = 293 | issue = 5538 | pages = 2248–2251 | year = 2001 | pmid =  11567137|bibcode = 2001Sci...293.2248G | s2cid = 234618 | url = https://digitalrepository.unm.edu/biol_fsp/2 | url-access = subscription }}</ref>

West has since been honoured as one of [[Time (magazine)|''Time'' magazine]]'s [[Time 100]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20060615073639/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,1187290,00.html Time Magazine's article about West]</ref> He is a member of the World Knowledge Dialogue Scientific Board.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20080503102946/http://www.wkdialogue.ch/ World Knowledge Dialogue]}}</ref>
